It is accepted as democratic when public offices are allocated by lot; and as oligarchic when they are filled by election. - Aristotle, Politics 4.1294be

There are also less radical ideas for voting reform. One of the major problems with the current voting system is the possibility of a third party spoiler. Here is an example of how our current voting system prevents third parties from gaining momentum. Votes are split between similar candidates to the benefit of their mutual opponent. A necessary condition to eliminate vote splitting, and the spoiler effect is to allow voters to express their opinion about more than one candidate.

One system that satisfies the criteria for eliminating the spoiler effect is called Approval Voting. It is a simple and effective means to eliminate vote splitting.

Contact your representatives, and see what they think about eliminating the spoiler effect from elections.
